sample_unit: patients (retrospective cohort for model development); 42 patients in prospective pilot

links.outcome: Clinically meaningful pain improvement and VAS reduction, AI-assisted vs standard care in non-randomized pilot
links.effect: Improvement in 85.7% (18/21) vs 71.4% (15/21) (p = 0.449); mean VAS reductions 3.9 ± 1.2 vs 3.2 ± 1.4 (p = 0.092); not statistically significant.
links.quote: During a preliminary prospective feasibility implementation, clinically favorable numerical trends were observed in the AI-assisted group compared with standard care, including clinically meaningful improvement in 85.7% (18/21) versus 71.4% (15/21) of patients (p = 0.449) and mean VAS reductions of 3.9 ± 1.2 versus 3.2 ± 1.4 (p = 0.092).

screen.reason: The study develops and prospectively pilots a machine-learning CDSS prototype in a real point-of-care clinical workflow with 42 patients to assess feasibility. It evaluates the AI system itself rather than comparing outcomes with vs without an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
